description: This repo maintains its OWN toolchain, narrowly. It used to carry `enabled: false` (2026-06-03), which kept Renovate off it entirely — and the cost was measurable: its workflow actions drifted for months with nobody to notice.

The scope is deliberately narrow via `enabledManagers`: only `github-actions` and the custom manager below. `default.json` is the preset that the consumer repos extend UNPINNED from this branch, so main is production for them — it must never be moved by a bot. That holds twice over: no Renovate manager matches `default.json` at all, and `enabledManagers` excludes the `renovate-config` manager that would otherwise match this very file.

Everything is `automerge: false`. The single control is the packageRule below — `platformAutomerge` is NOT a guardrail, it only decides who performs the merge, not whether one happens. Drop that rule and the shared preset's automerge for patch/pin/digest comes back, on a branch that is production for every consumer.

The custom manager exists because the gate that protects the preset was itself unmaintained: ci.yml pins the validator with `npm install -g renovate@<version>`, and that pin sat a full major behind. A stale validator is a gate that has stopped seeing new rejections — so the thing that checks production now gets its own dependency PR.

customManagers.description: Keep the pinned renovate-config-validator in ci.yml current — it is the only gate over a preset the consumer repos extend unpinned.

packageRules.description: main is production for every consumer repo: each bump here gets human eyes.
